note: **10 and 12 Barrack Lane, schedules 17 and 16 of the 1939 Register, ED letter code RMGA, RG101/6177J.** A production manager and a bank cashier, each with servants - Barrack Lane in 1939 is not the mews the record has had it as.
source: 1939 Register, ED letter code RMGA, The National Archives RG101/6177J

census.occupation_at_census: Production manager and director, mechanical engineering works
census.source: 1939 Register, schedule 17, 10 Barrack Lane, ED letter code RMGA, Nottingham registration district 430-3, sub-district 26, The National Archives RG101/6177J - read from the page by A. Hagues; sub number 1; the page gives Production Manager & Dire Mechanical Engineering W, cut off at both ends. The record holds one other Houfton, a housemaid of 1891, and nothing to connect them. The house itself had been the Derrys' - a groom in 1881 and a jobbing gardener in 1901

1939 Register, schedule 17, 10 Barrack Lane, ED letter code RMGA, Nottingham registration district 430-3, sub-district 26, The National Archives RG101/6177J - read from the page by A. Hagues; sub number 2; seven months younger than George F and sharing his surname, so his wife

1939 Register, schedule 17, 10 Barrack Lane, ED letter code RMGA, Nottingham registration district 430-3, sub-district 26, The National Archives RG101/6177J - read from the page by A. Hagues; sub number 3; the index gives her as Cunnington (Gibson) (Loomes). She is single at 39 and ADA E CUNNINGTON at the next sub number carries no bracket at all, so Cunnington is the name the two were born with and the two brackets are marriages Gladys made afterwards

1939 Register, schedule 17, 10 Barrack Lane, ED letter code RMGA, Nottingham registration district 430-3, sub-district 26, The National Archives RG101/6177J - read from the page by A. Hagues; sub number 4; three years younger than Gladys A and sharing her surname, so most likely her sister - and it is her plain entry that fixes the direction of Gladys's brackets

1939 Register, schedule 16, 12 Barrack Lane, ED letter code RMGA, Nottingham registration district 430-3, sub-district 26, The National Archives RG101/6177J - read from the page by A. Hagues; sub number 1; the page gives Bank Cashier Mille Ban, the bank's name unread - Midland is the likeliest thing it stands for, and the page should settle it

1939 Register, schedule 16, 12 Barrack Lane, ED letter code RMGA, Nottingham registration district 430-3, sub-district 26, The National Archives RG101/6177J - read from the page by A. Hagues; sub number 2; twenty-two months older than George and sharing his surname, so his wife

1939 Register, schedule 16, 12 Barrack Lane, ED letter code RMGA, Nottingham registration district 430-3, sub-district 26, The National Archives RG101/6177J - read from the page by A. Hagues; sub number 3; the index gives her as Wakefield (Boyes). Nothing in this household settles which way the bracket runs, so she is entered under the surname in front, as the Cunnington sisters at number 10 are - but Boyes may be the birth name instead, and both are held
